name: Tedaga
sweep_summary: Tedaga is not in the catalog. The only title-sweep hit, Dybo 1994 (English, St. Petersburg Journal of African Studies 2: 29-50; 3: 27-44), has no open copy anywhere I could reach (inslav.ru posts only the Russian versions; archive.org, Crossref, Glottolog give no copy; S2/OpenAlex/Google Books APIs, WorldCat, HathiTrust, Google Scholar were rate-limited or blocked; Its Russian text, Dybo 1995 (MLJ 1: 236-279), was already on file from the daza1242 audit; I re-read the relevant pages by eye (pp. 238, 240, 263, 269), rendered fresh page images, and saved verbatim quotes with English translations at, logged in there. Dybo's finding: Tubu (Lukas 1953's data, chiefly Dazaga with Tedaga as 'northern dialect') has a paradigmatic, non-fixed accent governed by a Balto-Slavic-type contour rule -- stress on the first high-toned (dominant) syllable of the word-form; verbs divide into barytone (root-stressed, high-toned root) and oxytone (final-stressed, low-toned root) classes; Lukas gave no placement rule and the noun data are too thin. Tedaga-specific evidence is limited to three verb forms in fn. 18, p. 263, showing the same split. This is a Tebu-group statement from a secondary reanalysis, so for a Tedaga-proper coding the first-hand sources remain Lukas 1953 (De Gruyter, paywalled DOI 10.1515/9783112766194) and Le Coeur & Le Coeur 1956 (print only), both already flagged in this directory's earlier record. Acquisition priority for the 1994 English printing: medium (same content as the Russian text already read; useful only for quoting in English).

new_statements.quote: Die Tubusprache besitzt einen starken Akzent (Druck), der der Sprache einen energischen Charakter verleiht. In welcher Weise der Akzent rhythmisch im Satz verteilt wird, bedarf näherer Untersuchung. Der Ton spielt auch im Tubu eine nicht zu unterschätzende Rolle. [...] Es wäre aber trotz dieser Einschränkungen abwegig, die Bedeutung des Tons in der Tubusprache herabzumindern. Er besteht durchaus, sei es, allerdings in geringerem Umfang, als wortunterscheidender Ton oder sei es als formunterscheidender Ton [...] [Lukas 1953, S.7]. — Постановка ударения в словоформе, напротив, не вызывала у Й. Лукаса затруднений, поэтому все примеры в книге он акцентует, не давая, впрочем, какого-либо общего правила, которое определяло бы место ударения в словоформе.
new_statements.translation: The Tubu language possesses a strong (dynamic) accent, which gives the language an energetic character. In what way the accent is distributed rhythmically within the sentence requires closer investigation. Tone also plays a role in Tubu that should not be underestimated. [...] Despite these limitations it would be wrong to belittle the importance of tone in Tubu. It does exist, though to a lesser extent, as word-distinguishing tone or as form-distinguishing tone [...] — Placing the stress in the word-form, by contrast, caused Lukas no difficulty, so he accents every example in the book without, however, giving any general rule that would determine the place of stress in the word-form.
new_statements.citation: Lukas, Johannes. 1953. Die Sprache der Tubu in der zentralen Sahara. Berlin: Akademie-Verlag, p. 7 — as quoted in Dybo, V. A. 1995. Akcentuacionnye processy v jazykakh gruppy teda-kanuri i problema proiskhozhdenija paradigmaticheskikh akcentnykh sistem. Moskovskij lingvisticheskij zhurnal 1: 236-279, pp. 239-240.
new_statements.locator: Dybo 1995 p. 239 (Lukas quotation, ends '[Lukas 1953, S.7]') and p. 240 first paragraph; PDF p. 3 right half and p. 4 left half of
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement

Es wäre aber trotz dieser Einschränkungen abwegig, die Bedeutung des Tons in…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tubu (Lukas's description) is a tone language with a strong dynamic stress accent on top; Lukas marks the stressed high tone in every word but states no rule for where it falls, and says its rhythmic placement in the sentence is unstudied. Dybo's reading of Lukas's accented data (p. 240) is that stress is not fixed relative to word edges and that verbs split into a root-stressed (barytone) and an end-stressed (oxytone) accent type, i.e. lexically/morphologically assigned accent. No fixed-position rule exists in any source seen.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; Dybo (p. 240 fn. 2) notes Lukas does not describe accent behaviour in noun phrases and the material is too small to conclude anything.
new_statements.domain_note: Lukas's statement concerns the sentence (rhythmic distribution) and word-level tone; Dybo's accent types concern the verbal word-form. The description is of 'Tubu' as recorded by Lukas, i.e. chiefly the Keshirda dialect of Dazaga (daza1242) with Tedaga only as 'northern dialect' notes; nothing Tedaga-specific was accessible.
new_statements.identity_note: The only accent statement found is Lukas 1953:7 on 'Tubu', reached second-hand through Dybo 1995/1987 (held in the daza1242 folder). Lukas's Tubu is, per Walters 2015 (pp. 13-14) and Dybo's own dialect labels, chiefly the Keshirda dialect of Dazaga (daza1242), with Tedaga (teda1241) appearing only as 'Norddialekt' notes; WALS files Lukas 1953 and Le Coeur 1956 under Tubu = tebu1238 (the Tebu group). So the statement is a group-level (tebu1238) statement resting on Dazaga data, not a Tedaga-specific one. The Tedaga-specific description (Le Coeur & Le Coeur 1956, Tibesti Teda) was not accessible. The open Bardaï (Tibesti) orthography materials are Tedaga proper but say nothing about stress.

new_statements.quote: Внутренняя реконструкция (анализ системы в терминах акцентуационных валентностей и сравнение результатов с тоновыми схемами III глагольной группы), подтверждаемая непосредственным сравнением с тонами канури, позволяет установить, что акцент в тубу регулируется контурным правилом балто-славянского типа, т.е. акцент падает на начало первой последовательности морфем (соответственно, слогов) высшей валентности, иначе говоря, на первый слог с высоким тоном (соответственно, с восходящим или нисходящим тоном, которые приравниваются в контурном правиле к высокому).
new_statements.translation: Internal reconstruction (analysis of the system in terms of accentual valencies and comparison of the results with the tone schemes of verb group III), confirmed by direct comparison with the tones of Kanuri, allows us to establish that accent in Tubu is governed by a contour rule of the Balto-Slavic type, i.e. the accent falls on the beginning of the first sequence of morphemes (respectively syllables) of the higher valency -- in other words, on the first high-toned syllable (or the first syllable with a rising or falling tone, which the contour rule treats as high).
new_statements.citation: Dybo, V. A. 1995. Akcentuacionnye processy v jazykakh gruppy teda-kanuri i problema proiskhozhdenija paradigmaticheskikh akcentnykh sistem. Moskovskij lingvisticheskij zhurnal 1: 236-279 (Russian text of Dybo 1994, St. Petersburg Journal of African Studies 2: 29-50; 3: 27-44). Based on Lukas 1953, Die Sprache der Tubu in der zentralen Sahara.
new_statements.locator: p. 269 (PDF p. 18 right); supporting pp. 240 and 263 fn. 18
new_statements.reading: Word stress in Tubu is not fixed to a word edge: it is a paradigmatic (lexically/morphologically conditioned) accent whose position is predictable from tone -- the first high-toned (dominant) syllable of the word-form. Verbs split into barytone (root-stressed, high-toned root) and oxytone (final-stressed, low-toned root) classes (p. 240); no rule is statable for nouns (p. 240 fn. 2). Caveat on identity: Dybo's 'Tubu' is Lukas 1953's material, chiefly Dazaga (Keshirda); Tedaga enters only as the 'northern dialect' in fn. 18, p. 263 (hanā.nər.ín 'I don't know' vs barytone ráŋər.in 'I can't'; ké.dak.e.n 'he doesn't want'), which shows the same two-class pattern. It is a second-hand analysis of Lukas's accent marks, not fresh fieldwork on Tedaga.

sources.note: p. 239 quotes Lukas 1953:7: Tubu has a strong stress accent (Druck) giving the language an energetic character; how the accent is distributed rhythmically in the sentence needs closer study; tone exists but weakly. p. 240 (Dybo): Lukas accents every example but gives no general rule for the place of stress in the word-form; his verb data show two accent types, root-stressed (barytone) and end-stressed (oxytone). sources.note: Read in its Russian version (same work per Dybo's own bibliography, items 101/104/105). Dybo reanalyses Lukas 1953 (Die Sprache der Tubu), who accented every example but stated no placement rule. Conclusion (p. 269): Tubu accent is a paradigmatic (free, morphologically conditioned) accent governed by a Balto-Slavic-type contour rule -- stress falls on the beginning of the first sequence of dominant (+) morphemes, i.e. on the first high-toned syllable of the word-form. Verbs fall into a barytone class (root stress, high-toned root) and an oxytone class (ending stress, low-toned root) (p. 240);…
